ecosystem_hall_of_fame.name: Leonardo de Moura & Sebastian Ullrich
ecosystem_hall_of_fame.contribution: Created Lean 4, its kernel, elaborator, module system, and the v4.36 / v4.37-rc1 compiler speedups that make million-line verification possible.
ecosystem_hall_of_fame.bio: Co-founders of the Lean Focused Research Organization (Lean FRO) and chief architects of the Lean 4 theorem prover and programming language. Their work on the Lean 4 kernel, elaborator, module system, and recent v4.36/v4.37-rc1 performance improvements underpins both Mathlib and the formal verification of Alpoge's 17M-line RH/GRH proof.

ecosystem_hall_of_fame.name: Kim Morrison & The Mathlib Initiative
ecosystem_hall_of_fame.contribution: Stewarded Mathlib's library, tooling, and community infrastructure for years — and now runs RH's live distributed CI and merge queue.
ecosystem_hall_of_fame.bio: The Mathlib Initiative and long-standing leanprover-community maintainers built the unified mathematical library that defines `riemannZeta`, `RiemannHypothesis`, Dirichlet characters, and L-functions. Without Mathlib's vetted definitions, caching infrastructure, and reviewer culture, neither statement auditing nor community-scale cleanup would be possible.

ecosystem_hall_of_fame.name: Mario Carneiro
ecosystem_hall_of_fame.contribution: Formalized Lean 4's type theory (`lean4lean`) and built the export/checker foundations enabling independent verification outside the main compiler.
ecosystem_hall_of_fame.bio: Foundational Lean and Mathlib architect whose work directly anchors why mathematicians can trust Lean's kernel. He formalized Lean's type theory and kernel specification (`lean4lean`), helped shape `lean4export` and external kernel checking, and continues to advise on modularization and memory footprint at million-line scale.

ecosystem_hall_of_fame.name: Kevin Buzzard & Xena Project
ecosystem_hall_of_fame.contribution: Pioneered modern research-math formalization in Lean (LTE, FLT), onboarded a generation of mathematicians, and anchored public verification standards.
ecosystem_hall_of_fame.bio: Professor of Pure Mathematics at Imperial College London and founder of the Xena Project. Through projects including the Liquid Tensor Experiment and Fermat's Last Theorem in Lean, he brought working research mathematicians into the Lean community and set public expectations for transparent, kernel-checked verification.

ecosystem_hall_of_fame.name: Sébastien Gouëzel
ecosystem_hall_of_fame.contribution: Core Mathlib analysis and performance maintainer whose v4.37-rc1 23% Mathlib speedup report directly catalyzed RH's #185 toolchain bump.
ecosystem_hall_of_fame.bio: CNRS research director and one of Mathlib's core maintainers in analysis, measure theory, and build performance. His benchmark showing a 23% Mathlib compilation speedup on Lean 4.37.0-rc1 directly catalyzed the RH cleanup community's decision to jump straight to v4.37.0-rc1 in PR #185.

ecosystem_hall_of_fame.name: Andrew Sutherland, Szymon Teżewski & External Checkers
ecosystem_hall_of_fame.org: MIT · con-leche / con-agua / nanoda / Gruszka / Pestka
ecosystem_hall_of_fame.contribution: Independently compiled and replayed the 61 GB export across 6+ independent kernels (`con-leche`, `con-ron`, `con-agua`, `nanoda`, `Gruszka`, `Pestka`) and published `pp.all` Lagarias/Robin statements.
ecosystem_hall_of_fame.bio: Andrew Sutherland (MIT) led independent end-to-end compilation and 61.57 GB export verification (including Robin/Lagarias inequality equivalence and `pp.all` statement dumps at `math.mit.edu/~drew/grh/`), while Szymon Teżewski and external-checker authors verified the proof across independent languages and runtimes (`con-leche`, `con-ron`, `con-agua`, `nanoda`, `Gruszka`, `Pestka`, including exporter-free `.olean` checks).

ecosystem_hall_of_fame.bio: Long-standing Mathlib maintainers and Lean Zulip stewards including Johan Commelin (who published the official Lean community verification statement) and Eric Wieser (who organized and moderated the `#general` and `RH:` cleanup/toolchain/trust discussion streams under peak global traffic).
